frontMatter.introduction:
Jutify Lifestyle Private Limited recognises the potential environmental, occupational health, and safety risks associated with hazardous waste generated during textile and ready-made garment (RMG) manufacturing activities. Hazardous waste at Jutify Lifestyle may arise from operations such as printing, washing, dyeing support activities, chemical storage and handling, effluent treatment processes, maintenance activities, and utility operations. Typical hazardous wastes include chemical-contaminated sludge, used oils and lubricants, contaminated containers and drums, oily rags, chemical residues, and contaminated personal protective equipment (PPE).

This Hazardous Waste Management Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes a structured and comprehensive framework for the identification, segregation, handling, storage, internal movement, transportation, and final disposal of hazardous waste generated across all Jutify Lifestyle facilities. The SOP is designed to prevent environmental pollution, minimise occupational health and safety risks, ensure compliance with applicable legal and buyer requirements, and safeguard employees, contractors, surrounding communities, and the environment.

Aligned with applicable environmental regulations in India, recognised international environmental management practices, and the principles of ISO 14001, this SOP ensures that hazardous waste is managed in a manner that:
Minimises environmental impact and pollution risks
Promotes safe handling and controlled disposal
Protects employee health, safety, and well-being
Supports Jutify Lifestyle's sustainability, compliance, and ESG commitments
frontMatter.objective:
The primary objectives of this Hazardous Waste Management SOP are to:
Ensure safe, compliant, and traceable handling of all hazardous waste generated at Jutify Lifestyle facilities.
Establish clear procedures for identification, labelling, containment, and storage of hazardous waste streams.
Reduce hazardous waste generation through process optimisation, efficient chemical usage, preventive maintenance, and material substitution wherever feasible.
Define clear roles and responsibilities for hazardous waste handling, internal movement, and final disposal.
Support compliance with national environmental regulations, buyer environmental standards, and environmental management system requirements aligned with ISO 14001.

sops.title: Specialized Treatment and Safe Disposal of Hazardous Substances

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedures for the specialized treatment and safe disposal of hazardous substances at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd. The purpose is to ensure the proper handling of hazardous substances to mitigate environmental impact and comply with legal regulations.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party associates involved in the treatment and disposal of hazardous substances at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, including research and development, manufacturing, and distribution activities.

body.text: Hazardous substances requiring specialized treatment must be identified through safety data sheets (SDS) and classified according to their specific treatment needs.

Use specialized treatment methods such as neutralization, stabilization, or biological treatment as per the nature of the hazardous substances. Engage certified external service providers if necessary.
Maintain records of the treatment process, including methods used, quantities treated, and final outcomes. Ensure all records comply with regulatory requirements.
Dispose of hazardous substances using approved disposal methods such as incineration, secure landfill, or chemical treatment. Ensure methods align with environmental regulations and best practices.
Engage licensed waste disposal contractors for the removal and disposal of hazardous substances. Ensure contractors adhere to legal and environmental standards.
Maintain disposal records, including details of the substances, disposal methods, contractor information, and any regulatory permits. Document all disposal activities for compliance verification.

blocks.text: Regulatory Adherence: All procedures must comply with national and international regulations regarding hazardous waste treatment and disposal, including Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) guidelines.
Incident Reporting: Report any incidents involving improper disposal or treatment immediately to the safety officer. An investigation will be conducted, and corrective actions will be implemented.

responsibilities: The Safety Officer is responsible for overseeing the treatment and disposal processes, ensuring compliance with this SOP, and coordinating with disposal contractors.
The Environmental Compliance Manager is responsible for ensuring that all disposal activities comply with regulatory requirements and maintaining accurate records.

blocks.text: Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Head of Safety and Compliance to ensure it remains effective and up-to-date with current practices and regulations.

sops.title: SOP for Take-Back or Buy-Back Program to Collect Product for Remanufacture, Recycling, or Safe Disposal

blocks.text: As part of its environmental stewardship and responsible manufacturing commitments, Jutify Lifestyle Private Limited integrates responsible product-use and end-of-life (EOL) considerations into the design, packaging, distribution, and post-use management of garments, fabric samples, trims, and pilot or development batches. This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlines Jutify Lifestyle's approach to minimising environmental impacts associated with packaging waste, unsold or obsolete garments, returned items, damaged stock, and surplus inventory, while promoting circular material flows, traceability, and transparency across the apparel value chain.
The objectives of this Product Use and EOL Management framework are to:

sections.title: Actions Implemented to Reduce Environmental Impacts

steps.heading: Actions Implemented to Reduce Environmental Impacts

rows: Adoption of minimalistic, right-sized packaging for garment samples, swatches, and shipments; avoidance of PVC and complex plastic–metal composites.
Preference for mono-material, recyclable polybags, paper-based wraps, and cardboard cartons; labels printed using water-based inks.
Transition to biodegradable cushioning, corrugated fibreboard, kraft paper fillers, and paper tape in place of plastic-based fillers.
Use of lightweight secondary packaging materials to reduce logistics-related emissions.
Clean secondary packaging reused for internal transfers, buyer sampling, and laboratory testing where feasible.

blocks.text: To reduce the environmental footprint and material intensity of packaging, Jutify Lifestyle has implemented the following measures:

steps.heading: Reduced Material Usage in Primary Packaging

body.text:
Redesign of polybags and protective wraps using thinner yet durable material grades to reduce plastic usage while maintaining garment protection.
Elimination of unnecessary inserts and excess secondary packaging layers, particularly for samples and buyer submissions.

Standardisation of carton sizes for common garment categories to improve container utilisation.
Introduction of lightweight packaging materials that maintain structural integrity while reducing shipping weight and transport emissions.

Shift toward mono-material packaging formats to enhance recyclability.
Avoidance of PVC-based laminates and metallised films in new packaging designs.

Use of water-based or soy-based inks and non-toxic adhesives.
Minimalistic label designs containing essential information only, printed on recyclable or recycled paper where feasible.

blocks.text: To prevent surplus production and associated material, storage, and disposal impacts, Jutify Lifestyle follows structured production planning and inventory control mechanisms:

body.text:
Integration of historical order data, buyer forecasts, seasonal trends, and sampling feedback into demand planning systems.
Monthly cross-functional reviews involving merchandising, production, and supply chain teams to adjust production plans proactively.
Modular and flexible production planning to allow changes in order size or style with minimal waste generation.

steps.heading: Inventory Control for Raw and Finished Goods

body.text:
Implementation of FIFO and FEFO principles for fabrics, trims, and finished garments.
Digital monitoring of inventory levels and ageing to identify slow-moving or excess stock.
Limited initial production runs for new designs or buyer trials to validate demand before scale-up.

steps.heading: Waste Reduction from Returns or Obsolescence

body.text: Coordination with buyers and logistics partners to reduce returns, consolidate shipments, and align packaging volumes with actual demand.

sections.title: Regular Disposal of Products and Wastes

steps.heading: Regular Disposal of Products and Wastes

body.text:
Damaged, obsolete, or unsellable garments are segregated and evaluated for reuse, donation (where permitted), recycling, or authorised disposal.
Garments or materials contaminated with oils, chemicals, or hazardous substances are classified as hazardous waste and disposed of through authorised vendors.
All disposal activities comply with applicable environmental regulations and Jutify Lifestyle's waste management procedures.
Jutify Lifestyle collaborates with:

Authorised recyclers and waste processors for textile and packaging waste.
Buyers and brand partners on take-back, reuse, or recycling initiatives for unsold or returned items.
Packaging suppliers to co-develop sustainable packaging alternatives and end-of-life guidance.
Continuous coordination with authorised transporters and recyclers ensures full traceability of product and packaging waste streams.

Packaging and shipment documentation includes guidance on reuse, recycling, and responsible disposal where applicable.
Safety Data Sheets (SDS) or chemical handling information is provided for auxiliary materials supplied with products.
Buyers and partners receive documented guidance on return, reuse, or disposal procedures for samples and pilot batches.

Reusable cartons, pallets, and protective materials are circulated internally where condition permits.
Non-contaminated paper and cardboard packaging is segregated and sent for recycling.
Fabric off-cuts, yarn waste, and defective garments are routed to authorised textile recyclers.
Pilot batch return protocols are available for buyers to enable consolidated reuse or recycling.
Primary packaging designed or specified internally by Jutify Lifestyle undergoes structured optimisation, including:

Light-weighting: Reduction of wall thickness, dimensions, and material mass without compromising protection.
Material Simplification: Preference for single-material packaging formats.
Elimination of Non-Essential Components: Removal of unnecessary inserts and mixed-material elements.
Design for Recycling: Packaging designed for easy emptying, cleaning (where applicable), and disposal through standard recycling streams.
All optimisation activities are governed through documented SOPs, work instructions, and change management records.

sections.title: Design for Disassembly, Recycling, and Remanufacturing

steps.heading: Design for Disassembly, Recycling, and Remanufacturing

body.text: Jutify Lifestyle incorporates circular design considerations at the product level:

Ease of Disassembly: Garments and components designed to allow material separation without complex tools or irreversible joints.
Standardised Materials: Use of standard material grades to improve recyclability and recovery.
Material Transparency: Clear identification of material composition to support sorting and recycling.
End-of-Life Guidance: Disposal or recycling instructions provided to customers and partners.
To support circularity:

Customers may return used, unsold, or end-of-life products under defined take-back or buy-back arrangements.
Returned items are assessed for remanufacturing, material recycling, or safe disposal.
Recovery programs are governed through documented responsibilities, tracking mechanisms, and implementation records.

blocks.text: This initiative aims to:

Enable efficient product use with minimal waste and resource consumption.
Prevent degradation, damage, or unintended emissions during storage and handling.
Extend product life and functional performance.
Reduce environmental and health risks associated with improper use or disposal.
Support customer compliance with regulatory and sustainability requirements.

sections.title: Resource-Efficient Product Design and Microfiber Emission Reduction

blocks.text: Design Strategies for Reduced Resource Use

Optimised material selection to achieve performance at lower process intensity.
Functional designs enabling effective performance at reduced temperature, time, or water use.
Reduced dependency on repeated processing or additional consumables.
Enhanced durability to reduce rework and premature disposal.
Measures to Minimise Microfiber Shedding

Optimised fiber and yarn structures to reduce breakage.
Surface treatments that improve fiber cohesion without increasing environmental impact.
Improved fabric strength and tear resistance.
Evaluation of wash durability to limit fiber release over repeated cycles.

Testing and Validation

Performance and environmental improvements are validated through:

Product development reports
Laboratory and pilot testing
Comparative performance benchmarking
Durability and abrasion testing
Maintained records include:

Production and batch records
Disposal and recycling certificates
Transporter and vendor manifests
Packaging specifications and weight data
Demand forecasting and inventory ageing reports

Annual reviews of packaging and EOL performance.
Participation in supplier innovation and eco-design programs.
Evaluation of reusable or returnable packaging solutions.
Employee suggestion programs and periodic reviews focused on material efficiency.

All product use and end-of-life management practices at Jutify Lifestyle Private Limited comply with applicable environmental regulations, buyer requirements, and apparel industry best practices. The company ensures traceability, responsible handling, and transparent communication throughout the product lifecycle through collaboration with authorised vendors and stakeholders.

Jutify Lifestyle Private Limited has established a structured and systematic review mechanism to ensure the continued effectiveness, relevance, and improvement of its Product Use and End-of-Life (EOL) Management practices.
The Product Use and EOL Management framework is reviewed at least annually, or earlier in the event of:

Changes in applicable environmental regulations
Updates to buyer or brand sustainability requirements
Introduction of new product categories, materials, or packaging formats
Significant operational changes or process expansions
Reviews are coordinated by the EHS and Sustainability function, with inputs from Production, Packaging Development, Procurement, Supply Chain, Quality, and Compliance teams.

narrative.text: Key performance indicators (KPIs) are monitored to assess effectiveness, including:

Packaging material intensity and weight reduction trends
Percentage of recyclable or reusable packaging materials
Volume of surplus, returned, or obsolete garments generated
Recycling and recovery rates for textiles and packaging
Inventory ageing and waste reduction outcomes
KPI trends are analysed to identify improvement opportunities and risk areas.

blocks.text:
Internal audits and inspections verify adherence to documented SOPs, work instructions, and EOL management practices.
Findings from internal audits, buyer audits, and third-party assessments are formally reviewed and recorded.
Non-conformities, observations, or improvement opportunities are addressed through Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plans with defined responsibilities and timelines.

Feedback from buyers, recyclers, logistics partners, and packaging suppliers is reviewed to improve packaging design, take-back mechanisms, and disposal practices.
Customer feedback related to product durability, packaging usability, and end-of-life handling is considered during review cycles.
Review outcomes are presented during periodic management reviews as part of the environmental and sustainability performance agenda.
Approved improvement actions may include:

Packaging redesign or material substitution
Expansion of reuse or take-back programs
Updates to product design, labelling, or usage guidance
Enhanced training or awareness programs for employees
Documented updates to SOPs, guidelines, and procedures are communicated to relevant stakeholders and implemented through controlled change management processes.
Review records, KPI analyses, audit findings, CAPA logs, and management review minutes are maintained as documented evidence.
Records are retained in line with Jutify Lifestyle's document control and data retention policies and are available for regulatory inspections and buyer audits.

sops.title: Specific Approval Procedure for Sensitive Transactions (e.g., Gifts, Travel)

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedures for obtaining specific approval for sensitive transactions such as gifts and travel to prevent conflicts of interest and ensure compliance with company policies.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party associates involved in sensitive transactions at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, including gifts, travel, and other similar transactions.

substeps.text: Submission: Submit a written request for approval of sensitive transactions, including details of the transaction, value, purpose, and recipient.
Review: The request will be reviewed by the Compliance Officer and relevant department heads to assess its alignment with company policies and potential conflicts of interest.
substeps.responsible: Compliance Officer and relevant department heads

substeps.text: Decision: Approval or denial will be communicated in writing. Approved transactions must be documented and reported to the finance department.
Record Keeping: Maintain detailed records of all sensitive transactions, including approval documentation, receipts, and any correspondence related to the transaction.
Reporting: Report all approved sensitive transactions to the Compliance Officer for tracking and auditing purposes.

narrative.text:
Transaction Review: Regularly review sensitive transactions to ensure adherence to approval procedures and detect any anomalies or compliance issues.

Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Compliance Officer to ensure it remains effective and compliant with current regulations and company policies.

blocks.text:
Regulatory Adherence: Ensure all sensitive transactions comply with legal requirements and company policies related to ethical conduct and conflict of interest.

Incident Reporting: Report any issues or breaches related to sensitive transactions immediately to the Compliance Officer for investigation and corrective action.

responsibilities: Reviewing and approving requests for sensitive transactions
Maintaining records
Ensuring adherence to this SOP
Processing approved transactions

blocks.text: Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Compliance Officer to ensure ongoing effectiveness and alignment with company policies and regulatory requirements.

sops.title: SOP for Measures to Protect Third-Party Data from Unauthorized Access or Disclosure

blocks.text: This SOP details the procedures to protect third-party data from unauthorized access or disclosure to ensure data security and compliance with relevant data protection regulations.
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party associates handling third-party data at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, including data storage, access, and transmission activities.

body.text: 1.1. Access Controls: Implement strict access controls to limit data access to authorized personnel only. Use authentication mechanisms such as passwords, biometrics, and access badges.
1.2. Encryption: Encrypt third-party data both in transit and at rest using industry-standard encryption protocols to prevent unauthorized access during data transmission and storage.
1.3. Data Handling: Ensure that third-party data is handled with confidentiality and integrity, avoiding unnecessary exposure and sharing. Implement data masking where applicable.

2.1. Detection and Reporting: Establish procedures for detecting and reporting data breaches or unauthorized access incidents. Ensure that all incidents are reported immediately to the IT Security Manager.
2.2. Investigation and Remediation: Investigate all reported incidents thoroughly. Implement corrective actions to address vulnerabilities and prevent recurrence of data breaches.

narrative.text: 3.1. Regular Audits: Conduct regular audits of data protection practices to ensure compliance with this SOP and identify areas for improvement.
3.2. Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the IT Security Manager to ensure it remains effective and up-to-date with current data protection practices and regulations.

blocks.text: 4.1. Regulatory Adherence: Ensure that all data protection measures comply with relevant data protection regulations, including GDPR, CCPA, and other applicable laws.
4.2. Incident Reporting: Report any data breaches or security incidents immediately to the IT Security Manager and follow established procedures for remediation and notification.

responsibilities: Overseeing data protection measures, conducting regular audits, and responding to data security incidents.
Ensuring compliance with data protection regulations and managing data protection training for staff.

blocks.text: 6.1. Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the IT Security Manager to ensure it remains aligned with current data protection regulations and best practices.

body.text: 1. Integrity & Anti-Corruption: Review history of bribery, fraud, litigation, or unethical business conduct. Confirm commitment to applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and fair competition laws.

2. Fair Labour & Human Rights: Confirm absence of child labour, forced labour, bonded labour, discrimination, or harassment. Verify compliance with working hours, minimum wages, social security, welfare facilities, and grievance mechanisms.

3. Environmental Responsibility: Review environmental permits, waste management practices, and regulatory compliance status. Evaluate pollution prevention measures, emissions control, water and energy management. Verify relevant certifications (e.g., ISO 14001) where applicable.

4. Information Security & Data Protection: Review data security policies, confidentiality controls, and access management. Ensure protection of buyer information, product specifications, designs, and personal data.
5. Occupational Health & Safety: Verify safety training, PPE usage, accident records, and emergency preparedness. Assess compliance with applicable occupational health and safety standards.

sops.title: SOP for Company-Specific Actions to Avoid Road Congestions

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the measures Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd will take to minimize road congestion related to company operations, aiming to improve traffic flow and reduce environmental impact.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party associates involved in transportation and logistics activities at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, including those impacting road congestions.

substeps.text: Optimized Scheduling: Develop and implement scheduling practices to stagger delivery and pick-up times, reducing peak traffic periods and minimizing congestion around company facilities.
Route Planning: Utilize route optimization tools to plan the most efficient routes for transportation, considering factors such as traffic patterns and road conditions.
Coordination with Authorities: Coordinate with local transportation authorities to align company operations with traffic management plans and participate in road congestion mitigation initiatives.
Vehicle Maintenance: Ensure that company vehicles are regularly maintained and serviced to avoid breakdowns and traffic disruptions.
Driver Training: Provide training for drivers on safe and efficient driving practices, including techniques to reduce road congestion and fuel consumption.
Fleet Optimization: Monitor and analyze fleet operations to optimize vehicle usage and reduce the number of trips required, thereby minimizing congestion.
Traffic Analysis: Regularly analyze traffic patterns and congestion data to assess the effectiveness of implemented measures and identify areas for improvement.
Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Logistics Manager to ensure it remains effective and responsive to current traffic conditions and company needs.

blocks.text: Regulatory Adherence: Ensure that all actions taken to avoid road congestion comply with local traffic regulations and environmental guidelines.
Incident Reporting: Report any incidents related to road congestion, including traffic violations and accidents, to the Logistics Manager for investigation and resolution.

responsibilities: Overseeing the implementation of congestion reduction measures, monitoring traffic impact, and coordinating with local authorities.
Managing vehicle maintenance, driver training, and route planning to support congestion reduction efforts.

blocks.text: Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Logistics Manager to ensure continued effectiveness and alignment with current traffic management practices and company objectives.

This SOP establishes procedures for effective waste management at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd. It focuses on the reduction of internal waste through material reuse, recovery, and repurposing, sorting and disposal of waste according to waste streams, and mapping of waste streams to enhance waste management practices.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party associates involved in waste management activities at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, including waste generation, sorting, disposal, and stream mapping.

steps.heading: Reduction of Internal Wastes through Material Reuse, Recovery, or Repurpose

substeps.text: Material Reuse and Recovery: Implement practices to reuse and recover materials, including furniture parts and equipment components. Develop procedures for the regular inspection and refurbishment of these items to extend their useful life.

Repurposing and Repairing: Encourage the repurposing and repairing of used materials. Establish a system for evaluating and categorizing materials for potential repurposing or repair, including the refurbishment of damaged equipment and components.
Documentation: Maintain records of materials reused, recovered, or repurposed. Include details of the items, processes used, and outcomes to demonstrate adherence to waste reduction practices.

steps.heading: Internal Sorting & Disposal of Waste According to Waste Streams

substeps.text: Waste Sorting: Sort waste internally according to specific waste streams, such as recyclables, organic waste, hazardous waste, and general waste. Clearly label waste containers to facilitate proper sorting and disposal.

Disposal Procedures: Follow established procedures for the disposal of sorted waste. Ensure that each waste stream is directed to the appropriate disposal or recycling facility according to regulatory and company requirements.

Documentation: Keep records of waste sorting and disposal activities, including quantities of waste sorted, types of waste, and disposal methods. Ensure records are maintained for auditing and compliance purposes.

Waste Stream Mapping: Implement a waste stream mapping system to visualize the flow of specific waste types from their source through to recovery, recycling, or disposal. This mapping should identify key points in the waste management process and areas for improvement.

Assessment and Improvement: Regularly assess the effectiveness of the waste stream mapping system. Use the mapping data to identify inefficiencies, potential improvements, and to optimize waste management practices.
Documentation: Maintain updated waste stream maps and related documentation. Ensure that mapping reflects current waste management practices and supports continuous improvement efforts.

narrative.text:
Regular Audits: Conduct regular audits to ensure compliance with this SOP and effectiveness of waste management practices. Audits should include inspections of waste sorting procedures, material reuse practices, and waste stream mapping accuracy.

Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Environmental Compliance Manager to ensure it remains effective, up-to-date, and aligned with current waste management practices and regulations.

blocks.text:
Regulatory Adherence: Ensure that all waste management practices comply with relevant environmental regulations and standards, including local, national, and international waste management laws.

Incident Reporting: Report any issues related to waste management, including improper sorting or disposal, to the Environmental Compliance Manager. Investigate incidents and implement corrective actions as needed.

responsibilities: Overseeing waste management practices, ensuring compliance with this SOP, and maintaining accurate records of waste management activities.
Implementing internal sorting and disposal procedures, overseeing material reuse and recovery efforts, and assisting with waste stream mapping and assessment.

This SOP establishes procedures for controlling and reducing air pollution at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd. It outlines actions to prevent and mitigate pollutants from company operations affecting the local environment, including improvements in production processes, equipment efficiency, and other pollution control measures.

This procedure applies to all operations, employees, contractors, and third-party associates at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, who are involved in activities that could contribute to air pollution, including the emission of dust, particulate matter, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), noise, odor, light pollution, and road congestion.

body.text: Prevention and Reduction of Pollutants

substeps.text: Improvement of Production Processes: Enhance production processes to minimize the generation of pollutants at the source. Implement techniques such as process optimization, raw material substitution, and the use of cleaner technologies to reduce emissions of dust, particulate matter (PM), VOCs, SO2, NOx, and other pollutants.

Enhanced Equipment Efficiency: Upgrade and maintain equipment to improve efficiency and reduce emissions. Regularly inspect and service equipment to ensure optimal performance, reducing the emission of air pollutants.

Pollution Control Systems: Install and maintain pollution control systems, such as scrubbers, electrostatic precipitators, and catalytic converters, to capture and neutralize pollutants before they are released into the environment.

steps.heading: Control of Dust and Particulate Matter Emissions

body.text: Control of Dust and Particulate Matter Emissions

substeps.text: Dust Collection and Extraction Systems: Install dust collection and extraction systems in areas where dust and particulate matter are generated. Ensure that these systems are regularly maintained and operated at peak efficiency to capture airborne particles.

Water Sprinkler Systems: Utilize water sprinkler systems in areas prone to dust generation to suppress dust and reduce airborne particulate matter. Adjust sprinkler operation to optimize dust control while minimizing water usage.
Filtration Devices: Implement filtration devices, such as bag filters and HEPA filters, in production areas to capture fine particulate matter before it is released into the environment.

Formal Clean-Up Processes: Establish formal clean-up processes for removing dust and particulate matter from work areas. Ensure that these processes are conducted regularly and are effective in minimizing dust accumulation.

body.text: Reduction of Noise Emissions

substeps.text: Noise Control Walls: Construct noise control walls, such as greenbelt barriers or sound barrier blankets and panels, around noisy equipment or production zones to reduce noise emissions to the surrounding environment.

Noise Control Systems: Install noise control systems or equipment, such as acoustic enclosures, muffling controls, and silencers on exhaust air pneumatic equipment. Insulate specified production zones to contain noise within the facility.

Noise Monitoring: Regularly monitor noise levels at various points within and around the facility to ensure compliance with local regulations and to assess the effectiveness of noise control measures.

body.text: Reduction of Odor Emissions

substeps.text: Isolated Storage and Ventilation Techniques: Implement isolated storage for odorous materials to prevent the spread of odors. Use specialized ventilation systems to capture and filter odorous emissions before they can escape into the surrounding environment.
Odor Control Systems: Install odor control systems, such as activated carbon filters and biofilters, to neutralize odorous compounds in emissions before they are released.

steps.heading: Enclosure of Plant and Sulfur Absorption

body.text: Enclosure of Plant and Sulfur Absorption

substeps.text: Closed-Loop System for Sulfur Absorption: Enclose specific plant areas to create a closed-loop system for sulfur absorption. Implement company-specific equipment to recover sulfur originated from textile manufacturing, particularly viscose, to prevent sulfur dispersion.

Sulfur Recovery Equipment: Install sulfur recovery equipment to capture and recycle sulfur compounds, ensuring they are not released into the environment. Regularly maintain and monitor the equipment to ensure efficient operation.

blocks.text: Keep detailed records of actions taken to prevent and reduce pollutants. Include documentation on equipment maintenance, production process improvements, and pollution control system operations.

Maintain records of dust control measures, including the operation and maintenance of dust collection systems, sprinkler systems, and filtration devices, as well as the effectiveness of clean-up processes.
Document noise control measures, including the installation and maintenance of noise barriers and control systems, as well as noise monitoring results and any corrective actions taken.
Maintain records of odor control measures, including storage and ventilation practices, the installation and maintenance of odor control systems, and any odor complaints and responses.
Document the installation, operation, and maintenance of sulfur recovery equipment. Record the amount of sulfur recovered and any incidents of sulfur release.

narrative.text: Regular Audits: Conduct regular audits to ensure compliance with this SOP and the effectiveness of pollution control measures. Audits should include inspections of dust control systems, noise barriers, odor control techniques, and sulfur recovery equipment.

Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Environmental Compliance Manager to ensure it remains effective, up-to-date, and aligned with current pollution control practices and regulations.

blocks.text: Regulatory Adherence: Ensure that all air pollution control practices comply with relevant environmental regulations and standards, including local, national, and international air quality laws.

Incident Reporting: Report any issues related to air pollution control, including equipment malfunctions or breaches in pollution containment, to the Environmental Compliance Manager. Investigate incidents and implement corrective actions as needed.

responsibilities: Overseeing air pollution control practices, ensuring compliance with this SOP, and maintaining accurate records of pollution control activities.
Ensuring that all pollution control equipment is properly maintained, repaired, and operated according to manufacturer specifications and company standards.

sops.title: SOP for Controlling Employee Exposure to Extreme Climatic Conditions

blocks.text: This SOP establishes procedures to protect employees at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd from the risks associated with extreme climatic conditions, including excessive heat, cold, humidity, and other weather-related hazards. The goal is to minimize health risks and ensure a safe working environment under extreme weather conditions.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party associates at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd who work in environments where they may be exposed to extreme climatic conditions, both indoors and outdoors.

substeps.text: Risk Assessment: Conduct regular risk assessments to identify areas and tasks where employees are exposed to extreme climatic conditions, including high temperatures, cold, humidity, and other weather-related hazards.

Monitoring Weather Conditions: Establish a system for monitoring weather conditions, including temperature, humidity, and wind speed. Use reliable sources of weather information to anticipate extreme conditions and prepare accordingly.

Thresholds for Action: Set specific temperature and humidity thresholds that trigger protective actions. For example, implement heat stress prevention measures when the temperature exceeds 35°C (95°F) or cold stress prevention measures when the temperature drops below 5°C (41°F).
Hydration: Provide access to cool drinking water in areas where employees are exposed to high temperatures. Encourage frequent water breaks to prevent dehydration.
Shaded Rest Areas: Create shaded rest areas near work zones where employees can take breaks away from direct sunlight. Ensure that these areas are easily accessible and provide adequate seating.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Supply lightweight, breathable clothing and sun protection gear, such as hats, sunglasses, and sunscreen, to employees working in hot environments.

Work Scheduling: Adjust work schedules to avoid peak heat periods, typically between 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM. Consider implementing a rotational work schedule to limit individual exposure to extreme heat.

Heat Stress Training: Provide training on recognizing the signs of heat stress, including symptoms like dizziness, headaches, and excessive sweating. Train employees on first aid responses to heat-related illnesses.
Insulated Clothing: Provide insulated clothing, gloves, and headgear to employees working in cold environments. Ensure that clothing is appropriate for the specific cold conditions they will face.
Heated Rest Areas: Establish heated rest areas where employees can warm up during breaks. Ensure these areas are easily accessible and equipped with seating.
Warm-Up Breaks: Schedule regular warm-up breaks for employees working in cold conditions. Increase the frequency of breaks as the temperature decreases.

Cold Stress Training: Provide training on recognizing the signs of cold stress, including symptoms like shivering, frostbite, and hypothermia. Train employees on first aid responses to cold-related illnesses.

steps.heading: Measures for High Humidity and Wet Conditions

substeps.text: Ventilation Systems: Ensure that indoor work areas have adequate ventilation to reduce the effects of high humidity. Consider using dehumidifiers in enclosed spaces.
Waterproof Clothing: Provide waterproof clothing and footwear to employees working in wet conditions. Ensure that PPE is properly maintained and replaced as necessary.
Slip Prevention: Implement slip prevention measures, such as non-slip mats and proper footwear, in areas prone to wet conditions.

Emergency Procedures: Establish and communicate emergency procedures for dealing with extreme weather-related incidents, including heat stroke, frostbite, and hypothermia. Ensure that all employees are familiar with these procedures.
First Aid Kits: Ensure that first aid kits are readily available in all work areas, with supplies specifically for treating heat and cold stress. Regularly check and restock these kits.
Emergency Contacts: Maintain a list of emergency contacts, including local medical facilities, in case of severe weather-related incidents.

Record-Keeping: Maintain records of weather conditions, risk assessments, protective measures taken, and any incidents related to extreme climatic conditions. Ensure that these records are kept up-to-date and are readily accessible.

Incident Reporting: Report any incidents of heat stress, cold stress, or other weather-related health issues to the Environmental Compliance Manager. Investigate incidents and implement corrective actions as needed.

narrative.text: Regular Audits: Conduct regular audits to ensure compliance with this SOP and the effectiveness of protective measures against extreme climatic conditions.
Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Health and Safety Manager to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness in protecting employees from extreme weather conditions.

blocks.text: Regulatory Adherence: Ensure that all protective measures comply with relevant health and safety regulations, including local, national, and international standards for working in extreme climatic conditions.
Incident Response: Respond promptly to any incidents related to extreme weather exposure, including conducting thorough investigations and implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

responsibilities: Overseeing the implementation of this SOP, ensuring compliance with protective measures, and maintaining accurate records of all actions taken.
Ensuring that employees are equipped with the necessary PPE, are aware of the protective measures in place, and adhere to the procedures outlined in this SOP.

blocks.text: Annual Review: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Health and Safety Manager to ensure its continued effectiveness and alignment with best practices and regulatory requirements.

sops.title: SOP for Engaging with Businesses Owned by Minorities and Vulnerable Groups in the Supply Chain

blocks.text: This SOP establishes procedures to actively engage and collaborate with businesses owned by minorities and vulnerable groups in the supply chain of Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd. The aim is to promote inclusivity, support economic empowerment, and ensure diverse representation in the company’s procurement and supply chain processes.

This procedure applies to all procurement activities at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, including sourcing, vendor selection, and contract management, with a focus on including businesses owned by minorities and vulnerable groups in the supply chain.

steps.heading: Identification of Minority-Owned and Vulnerable Group Businesses

body.text: Develop and maintain a comprehensive database of suppliers owned by minorities and vulnerable groups. This database should include details on the type of business, products/services offered, certification status, and geographical location.

Verify the certification of businesses owned by minorities and vulnerable groups to ensure their eligibility for engagement in the supply chain. Acceptable certifications may include those issued by government agencies, industry associations, or recognized third-party certifying bodies.

Set specific supplier diversity goals to ensure a minimum percentage of the company’s procurement budget is allocated to businesses owned by minorities and vulnerable groups. Monitor progress towards these goals regularly.

Establish outreach programs to engage and build relationships with minority-owned and vulnerable group businesses. This may include attending networking events, participating in supplier diversity fairs, and collaborating with industry associations that support these groups.

Implement supplier development initiatives, such as training programs, mentorship, and technical assistance, to help minority-owned and vulnerable group businesses meet the company’s procurement standards and requirements.

Develop inclusive sourcing strategies that prioritize the inclusion of businesses owned by minorities and vulnerable groups in procurement processes. Ensure that these businesses have equal opportunities to compete for contracts and are not disadvantaged by barriers such as lack of access to capital or resources.

Incorporate criteria for evaluating vendors that emphasize the inclusion of minority-owned and vulnerable group businesses. This should include considerations such as social impact, community engagement, and alignment with the company’s diversity and inclusion goals.

Ensure that the evaluation process for selecting vendors is transparent, fair, and free from bias. Establish a review committee that includes representatives from various departments to assess proposals and make informed decisions.
Foster long-term partnerships with businesses owned by minorities and vulnerable groups by offering multi-year contracts, consistent orders, and opportunities for collaboration on new projects.

Monitor the performance of minority-owned and vulnerable group businesses in the supply chain regularly. Assess their ability to meet quality standards, delivery timelines, and other contractual obligations.

Generate regular reports on the progress of supplier diversity initiatives, including the percentage of procurement spend with minority-owned and vulnerable group businesses, and the outcomes of supplier development initiatives. Share these reports with senior management and relevant stakeholders.

Establish feedback mechanisms that allow minority-owned and vulnerable group businesses to provide input on the procurement process, identify challenges, and suggest improvements. Use this feedback to enhance engagement strategies and remove barriers to participation.

Conduct annual audits to assess the effectiveness of this SOP in promoting supplier diversity and inclusivity. Review procurement practices, supplier selection processes, and engagement initiatives to identify areas for improvement.

Annually review and, if necessary, adjust the supplier diversity goals to reflect changes in the market, business needs, and the availability of minority-owned and vulnerable group businesses in the supply chain.

blocks.text: 6.1. Regulatory Compliance:
Ensure that all actions taken under this SOP comply with relevant laws and regulations related to supplier diversity, anti-discrimination, and fair trade practices.
6.2. Contractual Compliance:

Include clauses in procurement contracts that require vendors to adhere to the company’s standards for supplier diversity and inclusion, particularly in relation to engaging minority-owned and vulnerable group businesses.

responsibilities: The Procurement Manager is responsible for implementing this SOP, ensuring the inclusion of minority-owned and vulnerable group businesses in the supply chain, and overseeing the monitoring and reporting processes.

The Supplier Diversity Officer is responsible for maintaining the supplier database, conducting outreach programs, and developing supplier diversity initiatives to support the inclusion of these businesses.

blocks.text: 8.1. Annual Review:

This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Supplier Diversity Officer to ensure its continued effectiveness in promoting the inclusion of businesses owned by minorities and vulnerable groups in the supply chain.

sops.title: SOP for Incentivizing Suppliers on Environmental and Social Issues

blocks.text: This SOP establishes the procedure for providing unique incentives to suppliers who demonstrate strong performance on environmental and social issues. The aim is to encourage sustainable practices, promote social responsibility, and enhance the overall sustainability of Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd’s supply chain.

This procedure applies to all suppliers of Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, with a focus on those who meet or exceed the company’s environmental and social performance standards. Incentives include supplier awards, preferred supplier program status, and access to Requests for Proposals (RFPs).

body.text: 1.1. Criteria Development: Develop clear and measurable criteria for evaluating suppliers’ environmental and social performance. Criteria should include compliance with environmental regulations, sustainable resource use, waste management practices, labor rights, community engagement, and other relevant factors.

1.2. Supplier Assessment: Conduct regular assessments of suppliers to evaluate their performance against the established environmental and social criteria. Assessments should include site visits, audits, and reviews of documentation provided by suppliers.

1.3. Scoring System: Implement a scoring system to rate suppliers based on their environmental and social performance. Suppliers who achieve a high score will be considered for incentives under this SOP.

2.1. Supplier Awards: Establish an annual Supplier Awards program to recognize and reward suppliers who demonstrate exceptional performance in environmental and social responsibility. Categories may include “Best Environmental Practices,” “Social Responsibility Leader,” and “Sustainable Supplier of the Year.”

2.2. Preferred Supplier Program: Create a Preferred Supplier Program that grants high-performing suppliers preferred status within the company’s supply chain. Benefits of this program may include priority consideration for contracts, extended contract terms, and higher order volumes.

2.3. Access to RFPs: Provide suppliers who excel in environmental and social performance with exclusive access to participate in Requests for Proposals (RFPs) for high-value contracts. Ensure that these suppliers are given priority consideration in the procurement process.

2.4. Incentive Tiers: Develop a tiered incentive system where suppliers are categorized based on their level of environmental and social performance. Higher tiers offer more significant incentives, encouraging continuous improvement among suppliers.

3.1. Supplier Communication: Communicate the details of the incentive programs to all suppliers, including the criteria for eligibility and the benefits of participating. Encourage suppliers to improve their environmental and social performance to qualify for incentives.

3.2. Supplier Development Programs: Offer development programs and resources to help suppliers improve their environmental and social performance. This may include training sessions, workshops, and access to best practices in sustainability and social responsibility.

3.3. Feedback and Collaboration: Engage with suppliers to gather feedback on the incentive programs and identify areas for improvement. Foster a collaborative relationship with suppliers to support their efforts in achieving better environmental and social outcomes.

narrative.text: 4.1. Performance Monitoring: Monitor the performance of incentivized suppliers regularly to ensure they continue to meet the environmental and social criteria. Suppliers who fail to maintain their performance may be removed from incentive programs.

4.2. Incentive Program Review: Conduct an annual review of the incentive programs to assess their effectiveness in promoting environmental and social responsibility among suppliers. Adjust the criteria, incentives, and program structure as needed based on feedback and performance outcomes.

blocks.text: 5.1. Compliance with Regulations: Ensure that all incentive programs comply with relevant environmental, social, and procurement regulations. Avoid practices that may create unfair competition or violate legal standards.

5.2. Supplier Compliance: Require incentivized suppliers to comply with Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd’s environmental and social standards as a condition for receiving incentives. Non-compliance may result in the revocation of incentives.

responsibilities: Overseeing the implementation of this SOP, ensuring that suppliers are properly evaluated, and administering the incentive programs.
Developing the environmental and social performance criteria, conducting supplier assessments, and providing support to suppliers in meeting the company’s standards.
